meta_description: Dubai Creek hotels from €66 in Deira to €233 at Raffles. Deira, Al Seef, Wafi and Creek Harbour compared on price, score, pool, breakfast and metro.
h1_main: 10 Best Hotels on Dubai Creek in 2026
h1_muted: (Deira, Al Seef and Creek Harbour Compared)
author_role: 10 Creek hotels compared on nightly price, score, room size, pool, breakfast and metro
lead: For most people the best Dubai Creek hotel is Mövenpick Dubai Creek in Deira: a 5-star with a rooftop pool over the water for €86 a night. On a tighter budget, Jannah in Deira scores 9.0 for €66. If you want a beach and an infinity pool, cross to Creek Harbour, where Vida Creek Beach costs €148, and for old Dubai on foot, Canopy by Hilton in Al Seef is €95.

We lined up 10 hotels across all three sides of the Creek (Deira, the Bur Dubai bank from Al Seef to Al Jaddaf, and Creek Harbour) and compared them on the price for the same night, guest and location scores, room size, pool or beach, breakfast cost and metro access. Use the filters to pick a side or a budget, or jump to the comparison table.

review: Mövenpick Dubai Creek wins because nothing else on this list gives you as much hotel for the money. €86 a night buys a 5-star room of about 45 m² on Banyas Street, right on the Deira bank, with a 9.2 guest score and a 9.1 for value. At that price it undercuts every other 5-star here by €50 or more.

The pool is on the roof, with the Skyview Pool Bar looking out over the Creek and the city skyline. Rooms face either the Creek or the city, and there are four places to eat, from The Great Oaks for breakfast to Buonissimo for wood-fired pizza. Spa, gym and free valet parking complete a full 5-star package.

It suits couples and first-timers who want the old-Dubai side of the Creek, the gold and textile markets 10 minutes away by car, and Dubai International Airport only 5 km away by metro or taxi. Compared with Jannah (#7), you pay €20 more for a bigger room, a rooftop pool and a much broader restaurant line-up.

Catches: the cheapest rate is room only (breakfast €22), the tourism fee of AED 20 a night plus 5% VAT and a 7% municipality fee come on top, and there is a refundable AED 500 cash deposit on arrival.

review: If the deciding question is "where can we swim", this is the answer. Vida Creek Beach is the only hotel in the comparison that is listed as beachfront, and it adds an infinity pool, a kids' pool and a hot tub. Guests rate it 9.3, the highest on this page, with 9.5 for cleanliness, comfort and staff.

€148 buys a Deluxe Room of 431 ft² (about 40 m²) with a balcony and terrace. Lagoon View rooms start at €162. Breakfast is rated exceptional and covers continental, American, Asian and full English plates at Origins, the single all-day restaurant.

Against its sister Vida Creek Harbour (#10), you pay €40 more for the beach, bigger rooms with balconies and a higher score. Against Address Creek Harbour (#4), you save €34 and keep the beach, but give up the 5-star spa and the club lounge.
Catches: it is a 4-star at near 5-star money, there is only one restaurant, and the old souks and Al Seef are a drive away across the Creek. Taxes and charges come on top of the nightly rate.

review: Raffles is the splurge on this list and it earns the price with space. €233 buys a 753 ft² (about 70 m²) Signature room with its own terrace, the largest standard room in the comparison, and butler service is available for every room. Guests score it 9.2, with 9.5 for cleanliness, comfort and staff.

The building is the pyramid by Wafi mall on the Bur Dubai side of the Creek. Inside you get a large spa with saunas and steam rooms, an outdoor pool, 7 dining outlets including the Japanese restaurant TOMO, and afternoon tea at Raffles Salon. The metro is close and the airport is 15 minutes by car.

Compared with Sofitel The Obelisk (#6), also at Wafi, you pay €77 more per night for a room about 26 m² larger with a terrace and butler service. Sofitel's €156 rate includes breakfast; at Raffles the cheapest rate is room only, and rates with breakfast and dinner start at €370.
Catches: it is not a waterfront hotel, extra beds for over-12s are AED 400 a night, and the AED 20 tourism fee, 5% VAT and 7% municipality fee come on top.

review: Address Creek Harbour is the polished 5-star of the new side of the Creek. €182 gets a 40 m² City View king room, an infinity pool, beach access and a full spa with sauna. Guests give it 9.0 overall and 9.2 for location.

Families get more here than at most city hotels: a kids' pool, a child-friendly buffet, entertainment staff and free cots up to age 3. Couples can book club rates that include breakfast, afternoon tea and evening canapés. The hotel sits 0.6 miles from Dubai Festival City and is 8 km from Dubai International Airport.

Versus Vida Creek Beach (#2), you pay €34 more for 5-star service, a spa and three restaurants, but the guest score is lower (9.0 vs 9.3) and the room is the same size. Versus Mövenpick (#1) in Deira, it costs more than double for the newer district, an infinity pool and beach access.
Catches: breakfast is €38 on room-only rates, the creek-facing rooms cost more than the city-facing ones, the airport shuttle is paid, and taxes plus the AED 20 tourism fee come on top.

review: Canopy is the pick if you came for the old creekside, not the new towers. It sits on Al Seef Street in Umm Hurair, the heritage stretch of the Bur Dubai bank, and guests give it 9.2 for location. €95 buys a 35 m² King Room with a Nespresso machine and access to a heated rooftop infinity pool.

The hotel has 200 rooms and suites, two restaurants (NYON all day, SKAFOS for Greek and seafood), a sauna, steam room and gym. Breakfast is only €19 on the cheapest rate, and rates with breakfast included start at €112.

Against Mövenpick (#1) across the water in Deira, it costs €9 more for a smaller room and a lower score (8.8 vs 9.2), but you sleep in Al Seef rather than on the busy Deira waterfront. Against Jannah (#7), it is €29 more for a rooftop infinity pool and a better location score.
Catches: there is no beach or kids' pool, Downtown is about 10 km away, and the AED 15 tourism fee, 5% VAT and 7% municipality fee come on top.

review: Sofitel The Obelisk is the best way to get breakfast without paying for it separately. The €156 rate already includes breakfast, in a 474 ft² (about 44 m²) Deluxe room, with a 9.1 score and 9.5 for comfort. At Raffles (#3), also at Wafi, the cheapest rate is €77 more and has no breakfast.

The hotel stands by Wafi on Sheikh Rashid Road with metro access, 7 km from Dubai International Airport. There is a heated rooftop pool with a pool bar, a kids' pool, a hot tub and a spa, plus five restaurants including Brasserie Boulud and Bijou Patisserie.

Run the numbers against Mövenpick (#1): Mövenpick with breakfast included starts at €116, so Sofitel costs about €40 more for a similar-size room, a heated pool and a bigger restaurant choice, but on the inland Bur Dubai side rather than the water.
Catches: children count as adults from age 5 and extra beds are AED 200 a night, which makes it expensive for families. Taxes and the tourism fee are added at booking.

review: Jannah Dubai Creek Hotel, the former Edge Creekside, is the budget answer on this page. €66 a night gets a 4-star room with a 9.0 guest score, and the hotel still has an outdoor pool, spa, sauna, steam room and hot tub. Breakfast is only €12 on top, the cheapest add-on on this page.
Rooms are compact at 312 ft² (about 29 m²) with city views and soundproofing. The airport is just 3 km away, which makes it a practical first or last night, and check-in starts at 14:00.
Mövenpick (#1) is the step up: €20 more gets a 5-star with 16 m² more room and a rooftop pool on the water. If €20 a night matters more than a view, Jannah is the better deal.

Catches: only one restaurant on site, no Creek outlook, and some of the cheaper refundable rates ask you to pay the hotel before arrival. The AED 15 tourism fee, 5% VAT and 7% municipality fee come on top.

review: Al Jaddaf Rotana is the space pick. €167 buys a one-bedroom suite of 861 ft² (about 80 m²) with a separate bedroom, living room, two bathrooms, a full kitchen and a washing machine. At about €2.09 per m², it is nearly as cheap per square metre as Mövenpick (#1), and guests rate it 9.2.

It is also one of the easiest bases for getting around: Al Jaddaf Metro Station is a 5-minute walk, and Downtown, the Dubai Frame and Festival City are close. On site there are three places to eat (TIMO, the Tea Room and the Aquarius pool bar), a pool, gym, sauna and steam rooms.

For families it beats the other 5-stars on policy: cots and extra beds are free under 3, extra beds are AED 100 from age 3, and only guests aged 18 and over pay adult rates. Against Hyatt Regency Creek Heights Residences (#9), you pay €31 more for a separate bedroom and 22 m² more space.
Catches: breakfast is €30 on room-only rates, the tourism fee can be AED 40–60 a night on the larger suites, and the Creek is not in view.

review: This is the apartment option for people who still want a hotel around them. €136 gets a 624 ft² (about 58 m²) studio with a full kitchen, dishwasher, oven and washing machine, and the studio comes with river, landmark and city views. The tower is attached to the Hyatt Regency Dubai Creek Heights hotel, and there are four restaurants on site plus an outdoor pool and spa.
Location works well for getting around without a car: the metro is a 5-minute walk, Wafi mall is 7 minutes on foot, and the airport is 4 km away. A mini mart in the tower helps if you plan to cook.

Compared with Al Jaddaf Rotana (#8), it is €31 cheaper for a studio rather than a separate-bedroom suite. Compared with a standard 5-star like Sofitel (#6), you get 14 m² more and your own kitchen, but no breakfast in the price.
Catches: check-in is only possible from 15:00 to 19:00 and check-out is by 11:00, there is an AED 200 refundable deposit, and its value-for-money score (8.7) is the lowest of the ten.

The trade-off is space and extras. The City View Deluxe room is 344 ft² (about 32 m²), there is an outdoor pool but no beach listed, and breakfast costs €27 on the cheapest rate. Three restaurants cover Middle Eastern, international and French food.
Two things make it stand out: it is the only pet-friendly hotel in the comparison, and guests give it a solid 8.9. It suits couples on a budget who want the new district rather than the Deira bustle.

guide.h2: Dubai Creek Hotels Compared Side by Side
guide.html:
All ten are priced for the same weeknight for two adults, cheapest room. Eight of them (all but Mövenpick and Canopy) were limited-time deal rates that night, some at 50–65% off (Al Jaddaf Rotana, Hyatt), so expect those to rise when the deal ends. The column that changes the picture is € per m²: the cheapest hotel is not the best value for space. Mövenpick (€1.91 per m²) and the Al Jaddaf Rotana suite (€2.09) give far more room per euro than Address Creek Harbour (€4.55).

guide.h2: Deira, Bur Dubai or Creek Harbour: the Three Sides of the Creek
guide.html:
"Dubai Creek hotel" covers three very different stays. Pick the side first, then the hotel.

1. Deira (north-east bank): old Dubai, lowest prices, closest to the airport

Deira is the busy trading side of the Creek. This is where the money goes furthest: Mövenpick Dubai Creek (#1) is a 5-star for €86 and Jannah (#7) is €66. Both are 3–5 km from Dubai International Airport, and Mövenpick is about 10 minutes by car from the gold and textile markets. Choose Deira for value, souks and short airport transfers. If you only need a bed near the terminal, our Dubai airport hotels comparison covers that job directly.

2. Bur Dubai side (south-west bank): Al Seef heritage, Wafi and the metro hotels

The opposite bank runs from the restored Al Seef waterfront inland to Oud Metha (Wafi), Dubai Healthcare City and Al Jaddaf. Canopy by Hilton (#5) is the Al Seef pick at €95 with a 9.2 location score. Further inland, Raffles (#3) and Sofitel (#6) sit by Wafi mall with metro access, and the Hyatt residences (#9) and Al Jaddaf Rotana (#8) are both 5 minutes on foot from a metro station. This side suits travellers who want heritage streets or big rooms and the metro, rather than a beach.

3. Dubai Creek Harbour (east bank, further upstream): new towers, pools and the beach

Creek Harbour is the new waterfront district 0.6–0.8 miles from Dubai Festival City. Hotels here are modern and pool-focused: Vida Creek Beach (#2) is beachfront with an infinity pool, Address Creek Harbour (#4) adds a spa and beach access, and Vida Creek Harbour (#10) is the cheapest way in at €108. Prices start at €108 here versus €66–86 for the two Deira picks, and Dubai Mall is about 10 km away.

Staying on the Creek puts the old town on your doorstep: if you want a guide for the souks, the abra crossing and the street food, our Old Dubai tours compared lines up 10 walking tours on price, tastings and length.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Creek Hotel Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Best value overall: Mövenpick Dubai Creek, €86 for a 5-star with a rooftop pool and a 9.2 score.
  • Lowest price that still scores 9.0: Jannah Dubai Creek Hotel, €66, plus €12 breakfast.
  • Families who want to swim: Vida Creek Beach (beachfront, kids' pool, 9.3) or Address Creek Harbour (kids' pool, entertainment staff).
  • Families who need space: Al Jaddaf Rotana, an 80 m² suite with two bathrooms and a kitchen for €167; under-3s stay free and only 18+ pay adult rates.
  • Old Dubai on foot: Canopy by Hilton Al Seef on the Bur Dubai bank, or Mövenpick on the Deira bank, 10 minutes by car from the gold and textile markets.
  • A special occasion: Raffles Dubai, a 70 m² room with a terrace and butler service.
  • Breakfast in the price: Sofitel The Obelisk, €156 with breakfast included.
  • Self-catering: Hyatt Regency Creek Heights Residences, a 58 m² studio with a full kitchen, if you can arrive between 15:00 and 19:00.
  • Travelling with a pet: Vida Creek Harbour is the only one here that accepts pets.

If you would rather be near Burj Khalifa than the Creek, see our Downtown Dubai hotels; for the city's top 5-star resorts, see the best luxury hotels in Dubai.

guide.h2: Practical Tips: Fees, Getting Around and What Costs Extra
guide.html:
What the nightly price does not include

On the rates we compared, a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the Dubai tourism fee are added to the nightly price. The tourism fee is AED 15 a night at the 4-star hotels here (Jannah, Canopy, Vida Creek Harbour) and AED 20 at the 5-stars (Mövenpick, Raffles, Address, Al Jaddaf Rotana), rising to AED 40–60 on Rotana's larger suites. Two hotels take a refundable deposit on arrival: AED 500 in cash at Mövenpick and AED 200 at the Hyatt residences.

Getting around

For the metro, the Bur Dubai side wins: Al Jaddaf Rotana and the Hyatt residences are each 5 minutes on foot from a station, and Raffles and Sofitel have metro access at Wafi. Deira is the side for the airport (Jannah 3 km, Mövenpick 5 km). Creek Harbour is the most car-dependent; Vida Creek Harbour runs a shuttle, and all three Creek Harbour hotels offer free parking.

Kids, extra beds and arrival times

Extra-bed charges range from AED 90 (Jannah) to AED 400 (Raffles) a night, Vida Creek Harbour has no extra beds at all, and Sofitel charges children as adults from age 5. Check the age rules on the card before you book. The Hyatt residences only check guests in from 15:00 to 19:00, so they are a poor match for late flights.

What to do from the Creek

A Creek hotel puts you close to old Dubai's sights. For an evening on the water, compare Dubai dinner cruises; for a guided day through the old town and the new skyline, see the best Dubai city tours; and if Burj Khalifa is on your list, our Burj Khalifa ticket comparison shows which time slot is worth paying for. For a day out of the city, compare desert safaris and check that pickup covers your side of the Creek.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay in Deira or Bur Dubai?
faqs.a: Stay in Deira for the lowest prices and the shortest airport transfer: Mövenpick Dubai Creek is a 5-star for €86 and 5 km from the airport. Stay on the Bur Dubai side for the Al Seef heritage quarter (Canopy by Hilton, €95) or for metro access and bigger rooms around Wafi and Al Jaddaf.

faqs.q: What is the best hotel on Dubai Creek?
faqs.a: For most travellers, Mövenpick Dubai Creek: a 5-star on the Deira bank with a rooftop pool overlooking the Creek, a 9.2 guest score and a price of €86 a night. The highest-rated hotel in the comparison is Vida Creek Beach in Creek Harbour (9.3), at €148.

faqs.q: Are there Dubai Creek hotels with a beach?
faqs.a: Yes, in Dubai Creek Harbour. Vida Creek Beach Hotel is listed as beachfront and has an infinity pool and kids' pool; Address Creek Harbour lists beach access with its infinity pool. The Deira and Bur Dubai hotels have pools only.

faqs.q: Which Creek hotels are closest to the airport?
faqs.a: The Deira hotels. Jannah Dubai Creek Hotel is 3 km from Dubai International Airport and Mövenpick Dubai Creek 5 km, with an airport shuttle on request. The Hyatt Regency Creek Heights Residences in Healthcare City is 4 km away. For more options next to the terminal, see our Dubai airport hotels comparison.

faqs.q: Which Dubai Creek hotel is best for families?
faqs.a: For space, Al Jaddaf Rotana: an 80 m² one-bedroom suite with two bathrooms and a kitchen for €167, free cots and extra beds under 3, and only guests 18+ charged as adults. For pools and a beach, Vida Creek Beach or Address Creek Harbour, both with kids' pools and free cots up to age 3.

faqs.q: How much is the Dubai tourism fee at Creek hotels?
faqs.a: On the rates compared here it is AED 15 per night at the 4-star hotels and AED 20 at the 5-stars, up to AED 40–60 for larger suites at Al Jaddaf Rotana. It comes on top of the room price together with 5% VAT and a 7% municipality fee.

faqs.q: Is Dubai Creek Harbour a good place to stay?
faqs.a: It is the best side of the Creek for pools and a beach and the newest hotels, with location scores of 9.2–9.4 for the three hotels here. It costs more than Deira (from €108 at Vida Creek Harbour versus €66–86 in Deira) and is about 10 km from Dubai Mall, so it suits a relaxed stay more than non-stop sightseeing.

methodology: We compared 10 hotels on all three sides of Dubai Creek: Deira, the Bur Dubai bank (Al Seef, Wafi, Healthcare City, Al Jaddaf) and Dubai Creek Harbour. Each is priced at its lowest live nightly rate for two adults on the same weeknight, in euros, alongside the guest score and location score, the size of the cheapest room (converted to m² and € per m²), pool and beach, breakfast cost, check-in rules, child and extra-bed policies, metro and airport distances, and the taxes and tourism fee added at booking. Hotels outside the Creek area were left out.
